title: Submission Candidate
description: Self-contained record describing a single candidate finding being considered for a bug-bounty / contest submission. Consumed by the submission-readiness gate. This artifact is deliberately decoupled from the detection pipeline's finding schema.

finding_id.description: Stable identifier for this candidate (free-form; e.g. 'SUB-001' or a finding ID copied by a human).

title.description: One-line title naming the root cause and concrete impact.

root_cause.description: The specific code/logic defect (which invariant is violated and why).

affected_contracts.description: Contract file paths or names that contain the defect.

affected_functions.description: Function signatures or names where the defect lives / is reached.

attacker_entrypoint.description: The exact external/public function an unprivileged attacker calls to begin the exploit. Empty/absent if no external entrypoint exists (reachability gate will flag).

attacker_capabilities.description: What the attacker must be able to do (e.g. 'call any public function from an EOA', 'supply a flash loan'). Used to detect out-of-scope assumptions (leaked keys, social engineering).

scope_status.description: Whether the affected asset is in scope for the target program.

in_scope_asset.description: The specific in-scope asset (contract/address/module) per the program's scope list. Empty if not mapped.

out_of_scope_risks.description: Known out-of-scope dependencies or assumptions the exploit relies on (e.g. 'requires compromised admin key', 'depends on third-party oracle outage'). Non-empty entries that the exploit DEPENDS on will trip the scope gate.

severity_justification.description: Worst-case and realistic-case impact MUST be separated.

program_table_mapping.description: Which row of the bounty program's impact table this maps to.

bounty_program_mapping.description: How the candidate maps to the specific program's rules.

impact_in_scope.description: Whether impact_category is listed as in-scope by the program.

privileged_roles_in_scope.description: Whether the program explicitly accepts attacks that require admin/governance privilege.

scope_reference.description: URL or quote of the program's scope/impact table.

call_trace.description: Ordered call path from attacker_entrypoint to the impact (each step a string). Empty if not traced (reachability/evidence gates flag).

state_transition.description: Named storage slots / balances before and after the exploit.

asset_delta.description: Concrete economic/security delta (amounts, percentages) proving the impact. Empty if not quantified.

poc_path.description: Path to the PoC test/artifact. Empty if none.

reproduction_steps.description: Deterministic, ordered steps to reproduce. Empty if absent.

duplicate_check_status.description: Result of searching local prior audit reports / internal findings.

known_issue_check_status.description: Result of searching the program's known-issues / prior disclosures / public docs.

prior_audit_overlap.description: References to prior audits / reports that overlap (each a string: report id + note). Non-empty raises duplicate-risk to human review.

false_positive_risks.description: Honest list of reasons this could be a false positive.

invalidating_conditions.description: Conditions that would invalidate the finding OR mark a forbidden testing method (e.g. 'requires mainnet attack', 'tested on public testnet', 'assumes fabricated price'). Forbidden-method markers trip the PoC gate.

defense_analysis.description: Each likely defense and why it fails or does not apply.

blocks_path.description: True if this defense WOULD block the exploit path.

why_it_fails.description: Why the defense does not actually block the path.

uncertain.description: True if the submitter is unsure whether the defense applies.

assumptions.description: Explicit assumptions the exploit relies on. 'fabricated'/'assumed' markers may trip the PoC gate.

evidence_links.description: Evidence anchors: code lines (file:line), log excerpts, test-output paths, artifact paths.

triager_summary.description: Human-readable summary written by the triager.

recommended_status.description: Status recommended by the candidate author. The gate recomputes this independently; mismatches are reported but the gate's computed status governs.

human_approval_required.description: MUST be true. The layer never autonomously submits; a human must approve before any submission.
